findings.claim: ADR-0009 states as a flat fact that SessionStart(source=compact) is 'the only re-injection point' and 'PreCompact cannot inject', but its own Delivery table three lines later routes Gemini, Copilot CLI and VS Code through a second re-injection point entirely: a PreCompact-style hook that writes `pending_compact` plus the next UserPromptSubmit hook that reads it. README §6 confirms these three agents never re-fire SessionStart after compaction at all, so for them the stated 'only' path is unavailable and the real mechanism is the one the ADR calls impossible three lines up.
findings.evidence: ADR-0009:13 'Only re-injection point: SessionStart with source=compact. PreCompact cannot inject.' vs ADR-0009:96 'Gemini, Copilot CLI, VS Code | the compaction hook writes meta("pending_compact:"+sid). The next prompt hook runs a DELETE … RETURNING'. README.md:69 'Gemini, Copilot CLI and VS Code do not fire SessionStart again after compaction.' v1 confirmed VS Code's adapter already registers a native PreCompact hook (`src/adapters/vscode-copilot/hooks.ts:27,41,58` HOOK_TYPES.PRE_COMPACT mapped to precompact.mjs), so the v2 'compaction hook' for VS Code is in fact a PreCompact hook, the exact event line 13 says cannot inject.
findings.fix: Rewrite line 13 to scope the claim: 'Only re-injection point for Claude Code, Codex, Qwen, ZCode: SessionStart(source=compact); PreCompact never injects there.' Then state the second path explicitly for Gemini/Copilot CLI/VS Code: PreCompact writes a pending flag, the next UserPromptSubmit hook performs the actual injection. Do not leave a universal 'only' claim standing next to a table that contradicts it.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: v1 PreCompact support for VS Code — 75ae6ae3 2026-03-05 'feat: multi-platform adapters, session continuity, hook scripts' (hooks.ts HOOK_TYPES table). ORIGINAL_INTENT: give VS Code a hook that fires before compaction since it has no post-compaction SessionStart equivalent. REGRESSION_RISK: if a reader (or an implementer) takes ADR-0009:13 literally and removes the VS Code/Gemini/Copilot-CLI PreCompact wiring because 'PreCompact cannot inject', those three agents lose all post-compaction state recovery — a regression against v1, which already had this working for VS Code. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no fallback chain per owner decision — the two paths must be named as two fixed, agent-keyed mechanisms, not a primary-plus-fallback pair.

findings.claim: README §6 declares exactly '4 canonical events' (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse) and says every adapter maps every canonical event to one native event — but ADR-0009's compaction design requires a 5th event (PreCompact, or equivalent) for Gemini, Copilot CLI and VS Code, which is never listed as a canonical event anywhere.
findings.evidence: README.md:63-65 '4 canonical events ... Each adapter maps every canonical event to one native event' (no PreCompact row). ADR-0009:95-96 Delivery table requires a compaction-triggered hook distinct from SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse for exactly those three agents. grep -n 'PreCompact|canonical event' across docs/v2 shows PreCompact named only inside ADR-0009, never in README's event list or TECH-SPEC's adapter tables.
findings.fix: Either add PreCompact as a 5th canonical event in README §6 (name which agents map it and which don't, matching ADR-0009's table) or, if it is deliberately left out of the 'canonical' set because only 3 of 10 agents have it, say so explicitly so the 4-event claim is not read as complete.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: v1 defines PreCompact per-adapter ad hoc (e.g. vscode-copilot/hooks.ts:27, Codex's codex-rs hooks, Claude Code settings.json PreCompact entry) with no single canonical-event abstraction — v2's README is the first place that tries to name a fixed canonical set, and it undercounts. REGRESSION_RISK: medium — an implementer following README's '4 canonical events' table to generate adapter hook registrations (the table format strongly implies codegen, consistent with ADR-0016's generated-matcher pattern) would omit PreCompact wiring for Gemini/Copilot CLI/VS Code, breaking the compaction recovery ADR-0009 depends on for those three. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: name PreCompact as a real, if partial-coverage, canonical event rather than folding it silently into 'the compaction hook' prose only ADR-0009 uses.

findings.claim: ADR-0011's v1-cleanup table gives VS Code a single footprint row — 'whole file `<project>/.github/hooks/context-mode.json`' — but v1's VS Code adapter also writes two data locations this row omits: `.github/context-mode/sessions/` (project scope) and the home-directory fallback `~/.vscode/context-mode/sessions/` used when no `.github` dir exists (v1 issue #649), plus it registers itself in `.vscode/mcp.json`, which `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` never touches per this table.
findings.evidence: ADR-0011:76 VS Code row lists only the hooks file. v1 source `src/adapters/vscode-copilot/index.ts:97-110` getSessionDir(): 'Prefer .github/context-mode/sessions/ if .github exists, otherwise fall back to ~/.vscode/context-mode/sessions/' with the override comment 'Issue #649: CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR wins'. `git log -S"CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR" -- src/adapters/vscode-copilot/index.ts` = fa6541fb 'fix(adapter): CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR universal storage override (#649)'. `.vscode/mcp.json` registration read/write at index.ts:213-243, never mentioned in ADR-0011's table (contrast: every other agent row in the same table lists a 'data' path, VS Code's does not).
findings.fix: Add the two session-data paths to VS Code's v1-footprint row ('data: `.github/context-mode/sessions/` or `~/.vscode/context-mode/sessions/`') and decide whether `ctx_doctor` should also flag a leftover context-mode entry inside `.vscode/mcp.json` the way it flags a user-added MCP entry for Claude Code.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: fa6541fb (#649) introduced the CONTEXT_MODE_DATA_DIR override and the .github/~/.vscode fallback split; original adapter from 75ae6ae3 2026-03-05. ORIGINAL_INTENT (fa6541fb commit body / in-code comment): let dev-container/CI users pin storage to a writable volume regardless of whether .github exists. REGRESSION_RISK: low-to-medium — if v2's detectV1('vscode') only checks the hooks file, a user's old session data under .github/context-mode/ or ~/.vscode/context-mode/ survives uninstall as silent disk bloat, inconsistent with every other agent's row which does clean its data dir. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: v1 cleanup is detect-and-report only (no silent edits per the table's own rule), so add the path to the detector, not an auto-delete.
